newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: U.N. provides food to Cambodians fleeing fighting.
newsitem.headline: U.N. provides food to Cambodians fleeing fighting.

text.p: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) on Monday distributed emergency food to Cambodians fleeing fighting in northwest Cambodia, officials said.
Four trucks loaded with 80 tonnes of rice and 75,000 cans of fish entered O'Smach from the Thai border, witnesses said.
"This is the second lot of rice and necessities that UNHCR has distributed to displaced persons in two weeks," a UNHCR official told Reuters.
About 24,000 people are in O'Smach, many living in poor conditions and fearful of the nearby conflict, officials said.

"I received a bucket of rice from UNHCR 10 days ago but now we have no more rice left. If they do not come back, we will die," said Tu Rith, a 38-year-old mother of six who fled from Samrong, about 40 km (25 miles) south of O'Smach.
She was living under a plastic sheet with her family.

Fighting has flared sporadically in Cambodia's northwest between government forces under the control of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and opposition troops loyal to ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Hun Sen overthrew Ranariddh, his partner in Cambodia's tense coalition government, in Phnom Penh on July 6.
Ranariddh's army fled into Cambodia's northwest, where they are making a last stand at O'Smach.
Government troops moved to within one km (half a mile) of O'Smach on Monday.
Over the weekend, Hun Sen's troops bombarded O'Smach with mortar and artillery, with shells landing four to five km (three miles) from the town centre.
One shell hit the market, killing one civilian and wounding two others.
Officials in the Thai army base in Chong Chum across the border from O'Smach said they will allow civilians to cross the border if the situation worsens.
"We are monitoring the situation closely and would allow the unarmed people to come in only if the situation gets more serious," said Lt. General Sorayuth Chulanond of the Thai army.
The UNHCR official told Reuters the agency would assist refugees if they came across the border.
"We may have to help them inside Thailand," the official said.
